solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drawing, say, provided that cool scam

parts.note: drawing is an example of art
if means provided that
to ice something is to cool it

explanation.surface: An art critic suspects a cool con dressed up as a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is crafty trickery, and a scam is a piece of such deception.

clue.text: Troubling time when your locks play up?

definitions.text: Troubling time when your locks play up?

parts.words: Troubling time when your locks play up?
parts.note: locks are hair, and a day when hair won't behave has become slang for any day when everything goes wrong

explanation.surface: A light complaint about unruly hair spoiling the day, with 'locks' tempting thoughts of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a day of general frustration, literally one when your hairstyle refuses to cooperate.

clue.text: Dodgy seer and novelist peer who conducts study

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of shape, so the letters of seer are rearranged

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer is a bestselling novelist who sits in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: A shady fortune-teller and a titled author are lumped together with an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges SEER into RESE. Jeffrey Archer is a British novelist and life peer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose job is to conduct systematic study or investigation is an investigator of this kind.

clue.text: Flipping tender god

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: tender, as of a bruise, means sore

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about a soft-hearted deity: 'flipping' as a mild curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British oath; it turns SORE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of love, so he is a god.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on current cab

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or burden them
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A demanding passenger making heavy demands on the cab of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car with a driver, the everyday vehicle of that name.

clue.text: Boss has little time in the South of France

indicators.note: in places the short time unit within the French word for the south

parts.note: sud is the French word for south
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An employer squeezes in a short break on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' is not the Riviera but the French word for south, SUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, as is a stud on a shield or door.

clue.text: Crown Office and judge, as reported, stick together

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for a crown, an old coin
O is the abbreviation for office

indicators.note: as reported signals that the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: A government legal office and a judge are said to stand united.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown Office' reads as one body but gives two abbreviations; 'as reported' makes HEAR into HERE. A crown was an old British coin worth five shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together as a unified whole, to bond firmly.

clue.text: Bribe comes from gross manoeuvre

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen
to ease something is to manoeuvre it gently into position

explanation.surface: A backhander arises from some crude manipulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is slang for money used to buy favours, as in greasing a palm.

clue.text: Somehow certain about old backlash

indicators.note: about places the shuffled letters around the abbreviation for old
somehow says the letters of certain are arranged in some way other than given

explanation.surface: A vague certainty about a past backlash.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal rearranges CERTAIN into REACTIN, which 'about' wraps round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong adverse response, a hostile counter-movement.

clue.text: Cracker in cupboard is hard

indicators.note: in says the word lies inside the run of letters cupboard is hard

explanation.surface: A biscuit kept in the cupboard has gone hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' looks like a biscuit, but it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracker is British slang for a stunning person, and a dish is a good-looking person too.

clue.text: Most casual money drops off in Indonesia and the rest

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter

parts.note: easy means relaxed or casual
tin is slang for money
a wind dies when it drops off

explanation.surface: A careless gambler's cash disappears somewhere in South-East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most casual' looks like a superlative, but 'Most' cuts EASY to EAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Indies is an old name for the islands of South-East Asia, with Indonesia at their heart.

clue.text: Communal website in which Enzedder gets odd bits mixed

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the New Zealander are swapped round

parts.note: an Enzedder is a New Zealander, nicknamed a kiwi

explanation.surface: A New Zealander contributing to a shared website with jumbled bits.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first and third letters, K and W, trade places: KIWI becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiki is a website that any of its users can edit collectively.

clue.text: Fear drongo larking about in top plot?

indicators.note: larking about is fooling around, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frightened Australian fool messing around on a garden scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A drongo is Australian slang for a fool. 'Top plot' is cryptic: a garden plot on the top of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of planted ground on the uppermost storey of a building is cultivated at the top.

clue.text: Sioux city where some invaders landed

definitions.meaning: a city named after a Sioux people, in Nebraska
one of the Normandy beaches where Allied troops landed on D-Day

explanation.walkthrough: Sioux City is a different town in Iowa; this city is named after a Sioux tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nebraska city takes its name from a tribe, and the D-Day beach shares that code name.

clue.text: Roughly work out with patron I partner

parts.note: a patron of a hotel or restaurant is a guest
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: Calculating approximately alongside a customer and a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To guesstimate is to make an informed rough estimate of a figure.

clue.text: Painter, eg, on run means to get up

parts.note: a painter is a mooring line on a boat, an example of a rope
a ladder is a run in a stocking or tights

explanation.surface: A decorator on the move finds a way to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' is not an artist but a boat's line; 'run' is a ladder in hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing aid of cord with rungs is a way of ascending, a means to go up.

clue.text: Other ranks died for reform

parts.note: other ranks are ordinary soldiers, the men as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers died in the cause of change.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend one's ways is to reform, to improve or put right.

clue.text: Cast in all but complete contentment

indicators.note: all but complete means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: heaven is a state of bliss and contentment

explanation.surface: An actor's company in a state of near-total bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a troupe of actors but means to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast something is to throw it, as one would hurl it overboard.

clue.text: With an expression of polite dissent pressure expert

definitions.text: With an expression of polite dissent

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Politely disagreeing while pressing a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition means 'with all due respect to', used when courteously contradicting someone.

clue.text: Reduce order

definitions.meaning: to make something smaller or shrink it
a formal order for goods or services, an agreement

explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to grow smaller, and a deal placed with a supplier is a binding agreement.

clue.text: Dodge a turn aptly out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters are not in their proper sequence

explanation.surface: Avoiding a turn that comes at an awkward moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip school without permission is to dodge lessons.

clue.text: Oppressive open country where wild animal holes up?

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or open grassland
a den is a lair where a wild animal hides

explanation.surface: A beast lurks in the countryside, making the atmosphere heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden skies or a leaden mood feel heavy and weighing down, like lead.

clue.text: Kid taking in new country

indicators.note: taking in places the abbreviation for new within the boy

parts.note: a kid is a youngster, a lad

explanation.surface: A child adopted into a fresh nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Land is a nation or territory, as in a foreign land.

clue.text: Artificial aluminium limb causing needless nervousness

parts.note: false means fake or artificial
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A metal prosthetic arm causes unnecessary jitters.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning that turns out unfounded causes fear for no reason.

clue.text: Fiddle with prawns pulling tails off

indicators.note: pulling tails off removes the final letters of the shellfish dish

parts.note: scampi are large prawns, often breaded

explanation.surface: Fiddling with shellfish while peeling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like fussing with food but means a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a dishonest scheme or swindle.

clue.text: Copy No. 10's tip

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Imitating a tip-off from Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 10' suggests Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence, but is just the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the top or highest point, the peak.

clue.text: Guarantee to conceal payment

indicators.note: to conceal says the word sits hidden within the given word

explanation.surface: A security pledge hides a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot before a poker hand, a kind of upfront contribution.

clue.text: River launch

definitions.meaning: to launch is to throw or shoot forward, as with a small missile

explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a Devon waterway, and to dart is to propel or shoot, like a launch.

clue.text: Ultimate state of readiness on valley — right

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: Troops at the highest level of preparedness about a valley's right flank.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest alert level means maximum readiness for an emergency.

clue.text: Fish circling river's deep depression

indicators.note: circling places the fish around the abbreviation for river

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fish swimming round in the depths of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep depression' sounds like gloom but is a long ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, a deep cut in the ground.
